en.html:
...After that, a little over two weeks went by like a gale.

Persuade the senior house.
Obtain permission—grudging permission, but permission—for the masterless warriors to settle.

With my foster mother, explain it to the townspeople.
From most of them, a welcome.

The chief had returned to the mountain. No opportunity to meet her, but the 'bandit' raids stopped completely.

After so long, peace in the town again.
Even the senior house acknowledged my part in it.

As promised, arrangements were made to bring a doctor from Germany.

And then.
With his many instruments and assistants, the famous doctor came to our country town in Yamato—

en.html:
The improvement in Hikaru's condition was plain to see. Her lost hair had not returned, nor the flesh she had wasted away. But that shadow of death always beside her, that feeling of despair—somewhere it had gone.

No more animal-like groaning from her mouth.
Her breathing was entirely peaceful.

...But.
The eyes alone, no change.

Dark.
Empty.
Seeing nothing.

Glass-colored eyes. Where her mind was, they gave no indication.
Those were as before. Exactly as before.

Dr. Mengele"Dekhiye, one of the terrors of Jiibasu Bee—this pseudo-bacterial mineral poisoning—is the unceasing pain. Even medication has its limit. Such extreme pain eats away at the patient's mind..."
Dr. Mengele"The longer the delay in treatment, the more serious the damage. Confusion of memory, then loss. Changes in personality. Intellectual regression. Symptoms of mental fragmentation..."
Dr. Mengele"Ultimately, complete mental incapacitation."
Kageaki"............ Doctor..."
Kageaki"My sister?"
Dr. Mengele"..."
Dr. Mengele"One full year, a patient this gravely ill has survived with the medical care available in this country. That is remarkable. Your family's devoted nursing, certainly—and probably her own exceptional strength of body and mind as well."
Dr. Mengele"So a definite pronouncement, I will not make. A miraculous recovery is possible."
Dr. Mengele"...Physically, for the present there is no cause for worry. Complications from her weakened condition, those remain a concern. But as her body recovers over time, that danger too should be overcome."
Dr. Mengele"From my side, this is all I can do."
Kageaki"............"

en.html:
A miracle.

Never before had I examined that word properly. Today, for the first time.

And this I discovered.

Miracle. Such a pleasant sound. If you did not need one, it was winter clothing in summer. Very reassuring. Whenever winter came, protection was ready.

Need one, though, and winter had already come. Only now you discovered the almirah key was missing. The sweater was inside. Of what use?

Out of reach. It had been out of reach all along, and there you stood, stunned by this information.

The word did not tell you where hope was.
Quite the opposite.

What a miracle showed you...
was the hopeless distance still to go.

奇跡。

　その一語について深く考えた事など無かった。
　今日が初めてだ。

　そうして、気付いた事がある。
　奇跡。何やら耳に心地良いこの単語は、それを必要
としない者にとっては言うなれば夏場の冬着――いつ
か訪れる冬の寒さに耐える力を保証する心強いもので。

　必要とする者にとっては、冬になってから箪笥の鍵
を失くしたことに気付いて取り出せずにいる無意味な
<ruby>編服<rt>セーター</rt></ruby>のようなものだ。
　実は手の届かぬ所にあるのだと知って、唖然とする。

　希望の所在を示すものでは決してない。
　むしろ、その逆だ。

　奇跡が示すものは……
　そこに至るまでの、絶望的な距離だ。

en.html:
A miracle.
How to obtain one? This I did not know.

What should I do? Even that, I did not know. Before, there had been a definite aim: bring Doctor Mengele. After the promise to the senior house, settling the bandit problem had become the aim. A means to the first aim, but something I could work toward.

Now, no aim.
No—that was wrong. The destination remained. The road, I could not find.

What could I do...
to bring Hikaru's mind back?

...And before even that.
Could it really be brought back?

　　　　　—Why was I not called earlier—

Nothing else to say. So I said it.
An apology with no use and no meaning.

More than twenty years since the Minato family took me in. A life that should have ended by the roadside, they had kept alive. How to measure such a debt?

And my repayment? Look at it. I had not even saved the family's precious heir.

There was a limit to eating somebody else's grain for nothing. Why had I not been born as some more useful creature? If human requirements were beyond my capacity, livestock would have done. No objection from my side.

Compared with a man whose only achievement was finishing free rice, any nearby cow or horse was hundreds of times more valuable...

他に言葉がなく、そう口にする。
　益体もない、無意味な謝罪を。

　湊斗家に引き取られ、路傍に果てるべき命を生かさ
れて二十余年。
　その恩は形容しようもなく大きい。

　それに対して、俺の報いるところの少なさたるや。
　大事な家督継承者を救うことさえできなかった。

　穀潰しにも程がある。
　どうして俺は、もう少し役に立つ生物として生まれ
てこなかったのか。人間の器量に相応しくないなら、
別に家畜でも構わなかった。

en.html:
My foster mother's scolding was gentle. Unlike her fist.
But this was what woke me properly.

Giving up.
...Achha. So I had been giving up.

Despair at my own uselessness—what did that mean except deciding nothing more could be done? Giving up, only.

What nonsense.
Who had permitted me to give up?

Had it been my own life, perhaps abandoning it would have been my affair. But the life at stake was Hikaru's.

My permission alone, and I could throw it away? She had endured this whole year! Her will to live had astonished even the doctor!

Now even the time spent hanging my head felt wasteful. If I had spare time for that—

　それこそ、俺の目を覚まさせてくれた。

　諦め。
　……そうか。俺は諦めていたのか。

　自分の無力に絶望するという事はつまり、
　自分にはもう何もできないと、諦めるという事。

　そう思えば、項垂れている暇さえ惜しい。
　そんな余裕があるなら――

Subaru"You are going to save Hikaru. Me and you."
Kageaki"Yes."
Subaru"You are saving her. Because of you, Hikaru's body is better for now."
Kageaki"..."
Subaru"Thank you, I will not say. Apne ghar ki baat hai. She's family. Naturally we do this."
Kageaki"Yes...!"
Subaru"We see it through. And listen to me: you haven't gone backward. You haven't rolled all the way down either."
Subaru"You are moving forward. Believe that much."
Kageaki"..."
Subaru"Now you stand here looking behind you—hai, should have taken that other road. What will come of that? Aage dekh, beta. In front. That's where we're going."
Kageaki"Yes. I had no time to stand still."

en.html:
I nodded hard. Yes. Forward, even if I had to feel for every step. That was the work now.

Stand terrified because the road was dark, and what would change? Nothing! Collect similar cases. Look for recoveries among them. Find what treatments had helped. Work was not in short supply.

Instead of inspecting the garden like an idiot, I should have started on whatever was possible.
...This weakness of mine. Truly, it left me speechless.
